member.summary: CdoId: 1000; FieldId: 6184; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. member.name: P:Container.Workstation
member.summary:
CdoId: 1040; FieldId: 25853; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:Service.CIOAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 1080; FieldId: 673187932; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:CurrentStatus.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 2140; FieldId: 5154; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:CurrentStatus.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 2140; FieldId: 1353; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:CurrentStatus.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 2140; FieldId: 2643; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.summary:
CdoId: 2140; FieldId: 25854; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:HistoryMainline.ResourceStatusReason
member.summary: CdoId: 2440; FieldId: 25547; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. member.name: P:HistoryMainline.ReversalStatus
member.summary:
CdoId: 2440; FieldId: 4843; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: The status of this record in relation to Transaction Reversal. Values are: 1 = "Active" A non-reversed transaction has been executed. The ReversalStatus is initially set to this value for all committed transactions.
2 = "Deleted" A reversal transaction has been executed. Once a transaction has been reversed, it's original HistoryMainline record is preserved, but the "ReversalStatus" is changed to deleted.
3 = "Reversal" A reversal transaction has been executed. A new HistoryMainline record is created for each "deleted" transaction. The data of the new HistoryMainline is based on the original transaction data, but the ReversalStatus is set to "Reversal". The User and DateTime stamp reflect the details of the ContainerTxnRev service. New copies of the corresponding history summaries and history details are created for the reversed transaction. Fields (such as the quantity fields in the history detail) are negated that have the flag "Txn Reversal-Compensate" checked on the Properties advanced tab. The "deleted" record will have a positive quantity, and the "reversal" record will have a negative quantity, and when summed (ie:reporting), the total will be zero.

member.name: P:HistoryMainline.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 2440; FieldId: 7679; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.

member.name: P:HistoryMainline.Workstation
member.summary:
CdoId: 2440; FieldId: 25855; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. member.name: P:TrackableObjectCurrentStatus.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8487; FieldId: 22618; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: BusinessProcessWorkflow

member.name: P:ChangePkgCurrentStatus.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8488; FieldId: 22621; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: ChangeMgtWorkflow

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:Event.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 7489; FieldId: 12643; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:SampleTypeEnum.Counted
member.summary: CdoId: 8428; FieldId: 21659; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: For sample data collected of this type, the user must enter the number of samples taken during transaction execution. The user enters a count for each data point (reject type). All data point values are summed to arrive at the total number of rejects. Counted Sample Test never have data point limits configured.

member.name: P:SampleTypeEnum.Measured
member.summary: CdoId: 8428; FieldId: 21660; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: For sample data collected of this type, each data point represents a single sample. Data points are configured with limits. Data point limit failures are recorded as Rejects (one possible Reject per data point). All data point limit violations are summed to arrive at the total number of rejects. Measured data collections always have at least one limit configured for each data point.

member.name: P:NamedSubentityChanges.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 3735; FieldId: 16366; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:SessionValuesChanges.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 3740; FieldId: 7332; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:SessionValuesChanges.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 3740; FieldId: 10721; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SessionValuesChanges.ServiceTypeId
member.summary: CdoId: 3740; FieldId: 7329; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: CDO Definition Id of Default Service

member.name: P:SessionValuesChanges.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 3740; FieldId: 27696; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:SessionValuesChanges.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 3740; FieldId: 7331; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.name: P:TxnDetailsChanges.ReworkReason
member.summary: CdoId: 5230; FieldId: 4470; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Process Rework Code is used to provide a list of reasons for Process Rework. The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. This provides, for example, a means of differentiating between first pass and rework throughput in reporting. ; OriginalType: ReworkReason

member.name: P:TxnDetailsChanges.ToContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 5230; FieldId: 4473; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:CalendarShiftChanges.CalendarDate
member.summary: CdoId: 7052; FieldId: 8470; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift. For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day. A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:EventClassSpecMapChanges.Owner
member.summary:
CdoId: 8002; FieldId: 17505; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtlChanges.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8643; FieldId: 24838; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtlChanges.ToStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 8643; FieldId: 24846; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtlChanges.ToWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8643; FieldId: 24850; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27055; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27057; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.RecipeName
member.summary: CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27048; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Recipe Name

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27059; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.ResourceType
member.summary: CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27061; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Resource Type, a Resource categorization. Resources with the same Resource Type may share the same Resources Status Model.; OriginalType: ResourceType

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27067; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStep

member.name: P:KPIEntryChanges.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8857; FieldId: 27063; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

CdoId: 4726931; FieldId: 673187208; Workspace: 10; Flags: Exposed; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetailsChanges.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4752927; FieldId: 28533; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetailsChanges.Resource
member.summary: CdoId: 4752927; FieldId: 679493080; Workspace: csi; Flags: Exposed; Annotations: i) Sub-class of Resource. ii) No maintenance service. iii) Provides common fields to its sub-classes.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetailsChanges.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4752927; FieldId: 28531; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetailsChanges.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4752927; FieldId: 28535; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841486; FieldId: 702548289; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimesChanges.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841501; FieldId: 702546188; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimesChanges.ProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841501; FieldId: 702546187; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetailsChanges.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841502; FieldId: 702546199; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetailsChanges.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 4841502; FieldId: 702548215; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStepChanges

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetailsChanges.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841502; FieldId: 702546201; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetailsChanges.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841502; FieldId: 702546204; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStepChanges

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetailsChanges.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841502; FieldId: 702546203; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isRecipePlanDetailsChanges.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841624; FieldId: 702547468; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.summary:

It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isCompletedWIPSuummaryChanges.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841646; FieldId: 702547961; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: StepChanges

member.name: P:isOEERawDetailsChanges.isEmployee
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841505; FieldId: 702548003; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841505; FieldId: 702548008; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:isOEERawDetailsChanges.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841505; FieldId: 702547996; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isOEERawDetailsChanges.isProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841505; FieldId: 702547995; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

member.name: P:WIPMsgOperationKeyChanges.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 5140; FieldId: 4355; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:SpecSchedulingDetailChanges.FastCycleTime
member.summary:
CdoId: 4680; FieldId: 7124; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: This is a calculated value that denotes the time required processing a standard size batch of material using this Spec, assuming fast queue time. This is used to determine, for example, how quickly a job can be expedited through the Factory.
The calculation for this value uses attributes of other CDOs. This means that changing a Work Center value, for example, can effect this value. This means that this value should be calculated each time that it is needed. The value that is persisted will only be valid as of the point in time that this Spec was saved.

member.name: P:StepChanges.PathSelectors
member.summary: CdoId: 7098; FieldId: 9095; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Paths selectors are used to select a Path based on the value(s) of specific data within a transaction. Each Path selector includes an expression to evaluate and a Path to select. The expression to evaluate identifies a field (see note 1) to evaluate and a comparison value. The comparison value can be a single value, a range (from-through values), or a list of values. Expressions are evaluated in a defined sequence. The first expression that evaluates to true determines the Path to select.

member.summary:
CdoId: 7101; FieldId: 9141; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:ProductMaterialListItemChanges.PhantomBill
member.summary: CdoId: 6120; FieldId: 15810; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product. A Phantom Bill is a bill of material for a product that does not exist as an actual assembly, but is created only for the purpose of holding a group of related components. A phantom bill is created to reduce maintenance efforts, when such a logical grouping of components is used for many finished products, so that the maintenance of the logical group of components can be done in one place only. Note the Phantom Bill referenced on the material list item directly will ordinarily just be a pointer to a bill defined as part of the associated Product referenced by the material list item. ; OriginalType: BOM

member.summary:
CdoId: 6120; FieldId: 5618; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ProductEntity.isResolvedWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4740; FieldId: 702548207; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

CdoId: 4740; FieldId: 28658; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). member.name: P:WorkflowEntity.ERPRoute
member.summary: CdoId: 7099; FieldId: 9123; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.; OriginalType: ERPRoute

member.name: P:MasterRecipeEntity.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 7936; FieldId: 16789; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:SpecEntity.MaxQueueTime
member.summary:
CdoId: 4650; FieldId: 3956; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value determines the maximum length of time a Container can remain in an in-queue state at the Step that uses this Spec. The value for MaximumQueueTimeAction determines the action to take if the in-queue time exceeds this value.

member.name: P:SpecEntity.MaxQueueTimeAction
member.summary:
CdoId: 4650; FieldId: 3957; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value is used to determine the action to take when a Service (transaction) is started for a Container that has been in-queue longer than the allowable queue time (MaxQueueTime).
The values for this option are: 0 = No action 1 = Warning to Operator 2 = Warning to Operator requiring a password to continue 3 = Place container on Hold 4 = Do not allow transaction to continue
These values and their associated actions are intended to match the values and actions for field validations.
This action applies to any service that changes a Container from an In-Queue to an In-Process state.

member.name: P:MfgOrderEntity.isResolvedWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 3600; FieldId: 702547639; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:OperationEntity.SchedulingDetail
member.summary:
CdoId: 3780; FieldId: 3581; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Operation Scheduling Details
An Operation uses an instance of Scheduling Details to define scheduling information at the most generic level. Each value in the scheduling details can be overridden by a Spec (referencing the Operation). The calculation for cycle time is:
( ( (RunTime + SetupTime) / Utilitzation ) + MoveTime + [Fast/Normal]QueueTime ) [/ HoursPerDay]
The hierarchy built-in to the application model is that Scheduling details specified at the Operation level can be overridden by a Spec. In turn the values in the Spec can be overridden by each Step that references that Spec. It is also assumed that Scheduling Details will be overridden at the Product or Product Family level. Further, the assumption is that this will be for a few Steps (if any) and that adding user-defined fields to the Product or Product Family definition (and then updating the field overrides) will address it.

member.name: P:OperationEntity.ThruputReportingLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 3780; FieldId: 3587; Workspace: csi; Flags: Required; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:EMailDistributionEntity.EmployeeRecipients
member.summary:
CdoId: 7551; FieldId: 13132; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.summary:
CdoId: 8800; FieldId: 27709; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ShopFloorSettingsEntity.Level
member.summary:
CdoId: 8871; FieldId: 27189; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ShopFloorSettingsEntity.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8871; FieldId: 27193; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.summary:
CdoId: 4726896; FieldId: 673186860; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:CIOMessageTypeEntity.EventOnly
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726904; FieldId: 673187842; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: Channel Adapters can be configured for both inbound and outbound DoNotSend mode. In this mode, messages are buffered but the buffers are in offline mode. In this mode all calls to Peek or Get are ignored (thus not sending them on to their destination). In this mode, calls to Get Newest are processed and the newest message in the offline buffer is returned (also purging any older messages). The Get Newest is used to support the Get Message Web API call that is used by the Map Client.
This functionality is provided to allow specific messages to not be buffered nor sent to the Broker but to be available for SignalR Eventing (by subscribed clients).
This feature will add the ability to designate a specific message type as being EventOnly even when processed by an Adapter that is not in this mode.

member.name: P:CIOMessageTypeEntity.InhibitEvent
member.summary: CdoId: 4726904; FieldId: 673187792; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: InhibitEvent – this is used to prevent a particular message from being published to a client, regardless of whether it fits the client’s filter criteria. This might be needed for a message with sensitive content

member.name: P:isPreactorScheduleChanges.isWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841484; FieldId: 702547186; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isInventoryLocationEntity.isParentResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841509; FieldId: 702547780; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isMaterialQueueEntity.isMfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841520; FieldId: 702547270; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:isMaterialQueueEntity.isOperation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841520; FieldId: 702547272; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isAutoStartSettingsEntity.isLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841584; FieldId: 702546950; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:CIOFileAdapterEntity.CIOMessageChannel
member.summary: CdoId: 4726909; FieldId: 673187011; Workspace: 10; Flags: Required; Annotations: A logical address for the CIO Messaging System. Messages pass through a Message Channel as they flow to or from the Message Broker. Channel Messages are converted to and from an internal Message format. This internal format carries metadata and message contents in Xml format with UTF-8 encoding. The Message Channel provides filter pipelines where both standard and custom filter plugins are processed against a message to alter its contents - including conversions to and from UTF-8. This provides an extensibility point to handle very specific customizations.; OriginalType: CIOMessageChannel

member.name: P:CIOWebAPIClientAdapterEntity.CIOProcessResponse
member.summary:
CdoId: 4727030; FieldId: 673188004; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: ProcessResponse: String enumeration indicating how to process a response.
Valid values are:
None: do not generate a response message. Non-Ok status will cause a retry.
Content: return a response message from the contents of the response if the status is ok. Non-Ok status will cause a retry.
Status: return a response message that contains the status code and reason phrase. Non-Ok status will cause a message to be generated not a retry.
ContentsOrStatus: return a response message that contains either the contents. Empty contents or a non-Ok status code will return a response message containing the status code and reason phrase. Non-Ok status will not cause a retry.

member.name: P:CarrierFamilyEntity.isMfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 7909; FieldId: 702547790; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:CarrierFamilyEntity.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 7909; FieldId: 702547792; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isMfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 7908; FieldId: 702547782; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 7908; FieldId: 702547784; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7908; FieldId: 702547374; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isSingleProduct

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isSpec
member.summary:
CdoId: 7908; FieldId: 702547373; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:CarrierEntity.isTrackingContainer
member.summary: CdoId: 7908; FieldId: 702547368; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

member.name: P:isDeviceEntity.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841479; FieldId: 702546046; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:isDeviceEntity.CIOChannelSource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841479; FieldId: 702546042; Workspace: 20; Flags: None; Annotations: Channel Source
Messages can be sent to the CIO Messaging System directly, without use of a Channel Adapter. In this case, the Source system must interact directly with the exposed CIO Endpoints. The CIO Messaging System exposes a one-way service endp; OriginalType: CIOChannelSource

member.name: P:isDeviceEntity.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 4841479; FieldId: 675283052; Workspace: 20; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:SetSessionFilterTagEntity.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 8778; FieldId: 26102; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:SetSessionFilterTagEntity.EscalationRecipients
member.summary:
CdoId: 8778; FieldId: 26076; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:LotCurrentStatus.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4752651; FieldId: 679490864; Workspace: 40; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource
