member.name: P:CIOMessageService.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726999; FieldId: 673187714; Workspace: 10; Flags: Required; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:CIOMessageTypeMaint.CIOMessageChannelMaint
member.summary: CdoId: 4726875; FieldId: 673187970; Workspace: 10; Flags: None; Annotations: A logical address for the CIO Messaging System. Messages pass through a Message Channel as they flow to or from the Message Broker. Channel Messages are converted to and from an internal Message format. This internal format carries metadata and message contents in Xml format with UTF-8 encoding. The Message Channel provides filter pipelines where both standard and custom filter plugins are processed against a message to alter its contents - including conversions to and from UTF-8. This provides an extensibility point to handle very specific customizations.

member.name: P:CarrierMaint.isDocumentSets
member.summary: CdoId: 7914; FieldId: 702547802; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Document Set is a list of one or more documents. Most Modeling entities include a reference to a Document Set. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. member.name: P:ContainerTxn.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 2180; FieldId: 702547908; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:ContainerTxn.isProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 2180; FieldId: 702547909; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

member.name: P:ContainerTxn.isResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 2180; FieldId: 702548315; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isMaterialRequestTxn.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841590; FieldId: 702547013; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isMaterialRequestTxn.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841590; FieldId: 702547016; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:InlineSPCTxn.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8968; FieldId: 28575; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:MfgOperation.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8841; FieldId: 26844; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:MfgOperation.WorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 8841; FieldId: 26860; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:isManageInventory.isContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841512; FieldId: 702546302; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:BPMoveTxn.ToSpecStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 8499; FieldId: 22720; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: BusinessProcessSpecStep

member.name: P:StartChangePkg.Owner
member.summary:
CdoId: 8500; FieldId: 22306; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ProcessObjectTxn.DataCollectionDef
member.summary: CdoId: 7688; FieldId: 14959; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The Data Collection Definition used to define the parametric data fields to collect and place in ParametricData. If there is only one reference to this specific service in the Spec TransactionMap, InSite will fill in this field automatically. If a service exists multiple times in the TransactionMap, the user will need to input which data collection definition they are using. For instance, the CollectData service might be entered twice on the TransactionMap, once with parameters recorded every hour, and once with parameters recorded every ten minutes. member.name: P:PrintContainerLabel.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7309; FieldId: 10948; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:PrintContainerLabel.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 7309; FieldId: 10989; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.name: P:ReprintContainerLabel.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 7313; FieldId: 11003; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:ReprintContainerLabel.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 7313; FieldId: 11002; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.summary:
CdoId: 8079; FieldId: 18241; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:RemoteReceive.Container
member.summary: CdoId: 6975; FieldId: 7949; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) . A Container represent a grouping of other containers. The grouping allows a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. Containers are most often grouped together so a single workflow-oreiented transaction such as a move, movein, or transfer applies to the entire group of containers.

member.name: P:RemoteReceive.ContainerLevelName
member.summary: CdoId: 6975; FieldId: 7533; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Container levels are used to define a type of container, and will typically denote the position of the container within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Lot, Wafer, and Die would be defined as container levels. Attributes of the Container Level are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels.

member.name: P:RemoteReceive.ContainerStatus
member.summary: CdoId: 6975; FieldId: 7535; Workspace: csi; Flags: Required; Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

member.name: P:RemoteReceive.ToStep
member.summary: CdoId: 6975; FieldId: 7584; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: This object refers to the Workflow Step where the container is being moved to. If a path is provided, the path will override any information entered here. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:RemoteReceive.ToWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 6975; FieldId: 7583; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isLoadUnloadCarrier.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841615; FieldId: 702547371; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.

member.name: P:isLoadUnloadCarrier.WorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841615; FieldId: 702547355; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

CdoId: 3160; FieldId: 2967; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).

If there is only one reference to this specific service in the Spec TransactionMap, InSite will fill in this field automatically. member.name: P:Start.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 2400; FieldId: 28640; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:MoveIn.ToStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 2650; FieldId: 28718; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:MoveIn.ToWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 2650; FieldId: 28719; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:MoveTxn.OverrideCurrentStatus
member.summary: CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 2852; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: The intent of this field is to enable the client application to override the current status of the container (the step where the container is located at the beginning of the transaction). If the client application sets this field to "True" the transaction will assume the container is at the operation/step the client specifies, instead of using the operation/step of the container. This field should only be used for advanced automation systems where there is a virtual certainty that the automation system holds the correct information about the current location of the container. This allows the automation system to perform moves easily after the InSite has been taken offline and brought back up for database maintenance, etc. Note that there are no history records generated for the moves "missed".

member.name: P:MoveTxn.Path
member.summary: CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 2404; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Path defines an allowable (Standard) move from one Step to another within a Workflow. If a path is entered here, this path will override any information entered on the "Step" field. If no path or step is provided, pathselectors for the step will be evaluated to determine which path will be used. If no path selectors are valid, the container will be moved to the step referenced by the default path in the workflow.; OriginalType: Path

member.name: P:MoveTxn.ToSpecStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 2880; FieldId: 5801; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:ExecuteProductionProcess.ComponentIssue
member.summary: CdoId: 7219; FieldId: 29149; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Component Issue is used to select and (optionally) track which raw material lots or subassemblies were used at a particular manufacturing step. member.name: P:ExecuteProductionProcess.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7219; FieldId: 28124; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ExecuteProductionProcess.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 7219; FieldId: 28791; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.summary:
CdoId: 8982; FieldId: 28793; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ContainerHistoryInquiry.ContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 6908; FieldId: 7235; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:GetNCRs.ChargeToStep

member.name: P:GetNCRs.ChargeToWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 7220; FieldId: 10380; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:GetNCRs.Container
member.summary: CdoId: 7220; FieldId: 10375; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

It includes attributes for analytic data (Failure, Cause, Resolution, etc) as well as attributes to identify the material that failed (Container and component information).; OriginalType: NonconformanceReport

member.name: P:GetNCRs.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 7220; FieldId: 10376; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:GetNCRs.Workcenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 7220; FieldId: 10377; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.name: P:EligibleContainersInquiry.MfgOrderFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8191; FieldId: 19519; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:EligibleContainersInquiry.OperationFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8191; FieldId: 19520; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:EligibleContainersInquiry.ParentContainer
member.summary: CdoId: 8191; FieldId: 19521; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

member.name: P:EligibleContainersInquiry.ProductFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8191; FieldId: 19522; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:ProcessTimerInquiry.ProductFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8690; FieldId: 25252; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:ProcessTimerInquiry.SpecFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8690; FieldId: 25254; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:FilterTagInquiry.CurrentEmployee
member.summary:
CdoId: 8738; FieldId: 26038; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ProcessSPCChartDynamicParams.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8859; FieldId: 27043; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. member.name: P:CIOInquiry.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726863; FieldId: 673186734; Workspace: 10; Flags: Exposed; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).

member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.LineAssignment
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702547141; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.summary: CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702548048; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Represents, depending on context, an item or product that is required to complete a given manufacturing or assembly operation. member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.MfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702547142; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702548019; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702547197; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702547236; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isWorkOrderInquiry.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841602; FieldId: 702548020; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.summary:
CdoId: 8338; FieldId: 21325; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.summary:
CdoId: 8338; FieldId: 21324; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:MfgAuditTrailInquiry.ResourceFilter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8338; FieldId: 21326; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SessionValues.LocalSite
member.summary: CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 7985; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A site is defined as an independent InSite entity within a manufacturing organization. While a factory is a physical facilities concept, a site is a self contained IT structure based on a single transaction processing database, along with the associated InSite servers that provide the capability to generate transactions in the database. A factory could have one or more sites; and a site could run one or more factories.; OriginalType: Site

member.name: P:SessionValues.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 7328; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:SessionValues.Parent
member.summary: CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 3630; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Id of the CDO containing this CDO.; OriginalType: BaseObject

member.name: P:SessionValues.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 10720; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SessionValues.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 27695; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:SessionValues.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 1130; FieldId: 7327; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.name: P:HistoryDetails.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 2510; FieldId: 6726; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:CalendarShift.CalendarDate
member.summary: CdoId: 7051; FieldId: 8458; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift. For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day. A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

member.name: P:EmployeeRole.Employee
member.summary:
CdoId: 7782; FieldId: 15273; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:CategoryMap.Owner
member.summary:
CdoId: 7842; FieldId: 17500; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:CategoryNotificationMap.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 8098; FieldId: 19495; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:EventLog.Employee
member.summary:
CdoId: 8367; FieldId: 21390; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtl.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8642; FieldId: 24837; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtl.ResourceGroup
member.summary: CdoId: 8642; FieldId: 24839; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Named Object Group that represents a group of Resources.; OriginalType: ResourceGroup

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtl.ReworkReason
member.summary: CdoId: 8642; FieldId: 24841; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An instance of a Process Rework Code is used to provide a list of reasons for Process Rework. The code is associated with a Container when it enters a rework loop. It is then associated with all throughput transactions generated by the container while it is in the rework loop. This provides, for example, a means of differentiating between first pass and rework throughput in reporting. ; OriginalType: ReworkReason

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtl.ToStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 8642; FieldId: 24845; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ProcessTimerDtl.ToWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8642; FieldId: 24849; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:Timer.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 8678; FieldId: 25157; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27054; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27056; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:KPIEntry.RecipeName
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27047; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Recipe Name

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27058; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:KPIEntry.ResourceType
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27060; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Resource Type, a Resource categorization. Resources with the same Resource Type may share the same Resources Status Model.; OriginalType: ResourceType

member.name: P:KPIEntry.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27066; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStep

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27062; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:CIOOutboundDefinition.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726826; FieldId: 673186360; Workspace: 10; Flags: Exposed, ReadOnly; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28532; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Parent
member.summary: CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 679483733; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Id of the CDO containing this CDO.; OriginalType: ResourceLayout

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Resource
member.summary: CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 679483729; Workspace: csi; Flags: Exposed, ReadOnly; Annotations: i) Sub-class of Resource. ii) No maintenance service. iii) Provides common fields to its sub-classes.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28530; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28534; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

CdoId: 4841485; FieldId: 702548288; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimes.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841496; FieldId: 702546119; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimes.ProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841496; FieldId: 702546115; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546133; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546139; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702548213; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStep

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546141; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546142; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep
